next_step: Finish 2-week perf POC, technical readout, SOC2 scoping call
notes:
Overview: enterprise-scale realtime vendor building conversational and reranking features for web and edge clients. Strong latency/price sensitivity; will not accept >100ms p95 for chat route. Interested in Redwood's batching/caching/quantization tooling and benchmarking support.

Timeline / recent activity:
- 2024-11-15: Lead (Maya) inbound - CTO Rajiv Menon intro. initial requirements capture.
- 2024-11-20: Intro call (Fireflies FF-20241120- brickridge-intro). high-level perf targets: p50 20-40ms, p95 <=100ms for 128-256 token contexts; throughput target 200-400 reqs/s across bursts.
- 2024-12-05: Technical deep-dive with SE Diego Alvarez. looked at model variants (Mistral / Llama-family) and quantization tradeoffs. SE recommended perf benchmark harness + trace capture.
- 2025-01-08: Security questionnaire submitted (SOC2 + KMS + residency). Legal flagged data residency for EU customers.
- 2025-02-01: Agreed PoC scope: 2-week perf run comparing hosted vs dedicated with three configs: (1) fp16 baseline, (2) 4-bit quantized + KV cache, (3) int8-like fast path + aggressive batching. POC dataset: 12k real requests (anonymized).
- 2025-02-10: PoC started. Redwood to provide benchmark template and Jetpack config. Brickridge provided synthetic traffic + sample prompt set.
- 2025-03-05: Mid-POC checkpoint. initial numbers: hosted API baseline p95 ~ 180ms (unacceptable). Dedicated + KV prefix cache + small batching window (5ms) approaching p95 ~ 95ms for trimmed prompts. Quantized 4-bit shows token-rate improvement but needs quality regression checks.

Use-case & requirements summary:
- Workloads: conversational agents for customer-facing web UI (low-latency), reranking for search results (high-throughput), embeddings for personalization offline.
- Latency targets: critical routes p95 <= 100ms, p50 << p95 (goal p50 30ms).
- Throughput targets: 200-400 concurrent reqs/sec with burst capacity to 1k/s for short windows.
- Cost sensitivity: high. want to evaluate quantization and batching to reduce per-token cost while preserving output quality for core intents.
- Model preferences: open model variants (Mistral / Llama 2 family) with fallbacks to smaller, faster variants.
- Routing/fallback: must have deterministic fallback to a smaller model under load; need per-route latency SLOs.
- Observability: token-level cost, per-request traces, KV cache hit-rate, and quality/regression alerts tied to prompt tests.

Technical asks (explicit):
- Redwood to run benchmark harness and provide raw traces + per-kernel breakdown (compilation/kernel selection impact).
- Patch-level recommendations: batching window sizing (3ms, 5ms, 10ms), cache TTL and prefix/KV cache policy, quantization profiles (4-bit vs 8-bit) with sample quality metrics.
- Help instrument client-side telemetry for tail latency analysis.

POC success criteria:
- Achieve p95 <=100ms on chat route with <=20% quality regression vs fp16 baseline on core intents.
- 30-50% reduction in per-token cost through batching + quantization for reranking workloads.
- Reproducible benchmark report and rollback plan for canary rollout.

Quotes / call notes:
- CTO Rajiv: "We can accept a small quality delta but not at the cost of user experience — sub-100ms tail is non-negotiable for our chat flow."
- Head of Infra (Lena Park): "Need clear escape hatches and observability; if cache or batching causes wrong responses we have to detect and rollback fast."

Next steps / open items:
- Finish remaining PoC runs (int8-like fast path + canary routing).
- Schedule SOC2 scoping call with security team (Priya + Brickridge legal).
- Deliver benchmarking report and proposed Dedicated cluster topology.

Stitch / quick action items for AE/SE:
- AE Maya to confirm budget approval timeline with procurement (end of Feb).
- SE Diego to deliver KV cache tuning doc + quantization checklist by 2025-03-10.
- Book SOC2 scoping call - target week of 2025-03-17.
